title: Natural Selection and Evolution (KS4 Biology)
subject: Biology
strapline: How species change over very long periods of time.
facts: Evolution is the gradual change in the inherited characteristics of a population over many generations.
The theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by Charles Darwin.
Individuals in a species show variation, caused by differences in their genes (and the environment).
Those with characteristics best suited to the environment are more likely to survive and reproduce.
They pass on the beneficial alleles to their offspring — "survival of the fittest".
Over many generations, the beneficial characteristics become more common in the population.
Antibiotic-resistant bacteria (like MRSA) are a modern example of natural selection in action.

quick_quiz.q: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
What is the raw material for natural selection?
Give a modern example of natural selection.

teacher_tips: Teach the logical chain: variation → survival → reproduction → inheritance.
Use antibiotic resistance to show it is observable, not just historical.
Correct "individuals evolve" — populations evolve, individuals don’t.
